claims.hypothesis: CH3NCO is present in a low-mass protostar
claims.experiment: Line search in PILS data toward A and B
claims.result: 43 unblended lines toward B, 11 toward A; N ~3-9e15 cm-2
claims.finding: First detection toward a low-mass protostar, both components

evidence.quote: Methyl isocyanate is detected toward both components A and B of IRAS16293.
HOCN is not found down to \<3 $\times$ 10$^{13}$ cm$^{-2}$, giving $N$(HOCN)/$N$(HNCO) \> 1000

limitations_admitted.value: Pure CH3NCO could not be used for lab calibration due to toxicity; m/z 57/56 ratio differs from NIST

evidence.quote: methyl isocyanate is severely toxic and specialised laboratories and equipment are needed to work with this substance.

limitations_admitted.value: Data insensitive to cold CH3NCO since low Eup lines are missing

evidence.quote: Our data are not sensitive to any cold CH$_3$NCO component since lines with low $E_{\rm up}$ values are missing in the spectral range of the PILS survey.

reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The reduction recipe is inherited from another paper and the fitting details are incomplete; lab work is not reproducible from archive data.
